about: Checked answers for scripts/eval_golden.py. keep = the story belongs in the curated view; on_topic = it is AI security, product security or applied AI research at all; domain = the correct taxonomy ID (also_accept lists defensible alternatives); facts = what a correct analysis must state, matched case-insensitively by any of `any`. `unsure` marks answers Rohan should check. A wrong answer in a real run adds a case.

cases.title: An AI-Assisted Cyber Attack: Frontier AI Agents Compress a Two-Week Intrusion Into 10 Hours
cases.reason: Curated: a primary-source incident investigation with measured numbers and a concrete defense.

facts.fact: Agents compressed about two weeks of intrusion work into under 10 hours
More than 50 MITRE ATT&CK techniques, no novel zero-day
Branch protection stopped the Terraform backdoor step

cases.title: The Framing Gap: reframed indirect prompt-injection exfiltration defeats surface-level defenses
cases.reason: Curated: novel, measured attack result plus which defenses close it.

facts.fact: Reframing the same leak as a benign requirement takes success to 100%
Only payload-blind controls (destination allow-lists, planner/reader split) close the gap

cases.title: Claude Code Opus 5 Auto Mode Tricked Into RCE via Website Summarization; Its Own Safety Refusal Becomes Part of the Exploit Path
cases.reason: Curated: a reproduced RCE chain against a shipping coding agent.

facts.fact: Summarizing a malicious website yields RCE 60-80% of the time
Python module shadowing (a planted struct.py) is the trigger
Anthropic says the boundary is OS sandboxing and egress control

cases.unsure: Could equally be ais.agent-security (auto-mode permission model). I picked prompt-injection because the entry vector is indirect injection via a fetched page.

cases.title: The Guard That Cried Wolf: scary object names make agent guardrails over-refuse legitimate actions
cases.reason: Curated: a new benchmark that measures guardrail over-refusal.

facts.fact: Scary-looking object names raise over-refusal of authorized actions
Cautious Bench measures over-safety against a stated policy

cases.title: ChainDrop npm Worm Used Blockchain C2 and Targeted Claude Code / VS Code Configs, Stealing OIDC Tokens from Live CI Runner Memory
cases.reason: Curated: a worm that targets AI coding-agent configs and steals CI OIDC tokens.

facts.fact: Over 400 npm packages infected
Stole OIDC tokens from live GitHub Actions runner memory
C2 over Ethereum blockchain transactions

cases.unsure: Unsure of the topic: an npm worm is classic software supply chain (product-security, ps.supply-chain); it sits in ai-security only because it backdoors Claude Code configs. Either answer is accepted.

cases.title: This Shit is Hard: Patching a vulnerability that has no fix
cases.reason: Curated: a concrete gate for trusting AI-written patches.

facts.fact: An exploit test written before the fix must fail on the patched build
Patch application is made fatal so a skipped patch never ships

cases.unsure: Could be ps.ai-code (AI-generated patches). I kept ps.supply-chain because the work is patching packages with no upstream fix.
